# Risk-tier rules for bin/risk-tier. One rule per line:  <glob>   # <reason>
#
# This is a SAFE-LIST. A pull request is "phone-safe" only if EVERY path it touches matches a
# glob in the [safe] section at the bottom AND matches no laptop-only rule above it. Anything
# on neither list is "laptop-only": it needs a laptop review, not a phone merge. The laptop-only
# rules win over the safe-list, so a sensitive word in a docs or view path still flips the tier.
# Matching is case-insensitive and `*` crosses `/`, so `*consent*` matches any path with
# "consent" in it. Over-matching is deliberate: a wrong laptop-only costs a few minutes, a wrong
# phone-safe costs a defect. Why a safe-list: a list of sensitive names can only be as good as
# the memory of whoever wrote it, and gate round 2 found privileged files named
# web_controller.rb and test_helper.rb that no name rule would ever catch.
#
# A glob marked [forward] matches nothing in the tree today and exists for the day a file of
# that kind appears. Every other glob must match at least one tracked file; the test suite
# enforces it. This file itself is a rule target, so editing the rules is laptop-only.

# --- the machinery that decides what merges ---
.github/*                   # CI, CODEOWNERS, dependabot and these rules themselves
bin/*                       # executables, including the scripts that gate merges
*gemfile*                   # dependency set and versions (supply chain)
*.gemspec                   # dependencies and what the gem ships
Rakefile                    # task entry points that CI and releases run
.ruby-version               # runtime version the whole suite is judged on
SECURITY.md                 # security policy and disclosure contact
MIT-LICENSE                 # license text

# --- data shape and boot ---
db/*                        # migrations: irreversible once run against real data
test/dummy/db/*             # the schema the test database is loaded from
config/routes.rb            # adds or removes endpoints
test/dummy/config/initializers/*   # authentication and logging filters are configured here
config/initializers/*       # [forward] engine-level boot configuration

# --- authentication and authorization ---
*authentication*            # who is calling
*smart_*                    # SMART on FHIR launch, configuration and token handling
*backend_*                  # SMART Backend Services: system-to-system client auth
*assertion*                 # signed client assertions and their replay guard
*login*                     # sign-in and its throttling
*launch_context*            # what a launched session is scoped to
*kernel_user*               # the RPMS user a session acts as
*current_user*              # the user a request acts as
*site_gateway*              # site selection at sign-on
*e_signature*               # legal signature on clinical documents
*doorkeeper*                # OAuth server configuration
*oauth*                     # OAuth clients and access tokens
*token*                     # bearer tokens and token bridges
*jwks*                      # client key sets
*jwt*                       # [forward] signed assertions
*session*                   # sign-in sessions and session scope
*policy*                    # authorization policies, redaction and CSP
*compartment*               # patient compartment: what a caller may read
*authoriz*                  # authorization code, and the tests that pin it
*/ehr/application_controller.rb   # base controller: global before_actions, incl. FHIR scope authorization
*clinician_patient_context* # session-scoped patient binding, the cross-patient guard
lib/lakeraven/ehr/engine.rb # engine boot: Doorkeeper wiring and credential parameter filtering
*csrf*                      # cross-site request forgery protection and its probes
*rate_limit*                # brute-force and abuse throttling
*password*                  # [forward] passwords
*credential*                # [forward] credentials
*secret*                    # [forward] secrets
*permission*                # [forward] permission checks
*privilege*                 # [forward] privilege checks
*cipher*                    # [forward] ciphers

# --- consent, Part 2 and egress ---
*consent*                   # consent decides disclosure
*part2*                     # 42 CFR Part 2 substance-use-disorder segmentation
*part_2*                    # [forward] alternate spelling of the Part 2 surface
*segmentation*              # [forward] data segmentation
*redact*                    # redaction of what leaves the system
*egress*                    # everything that leaves the system
*bulk_export*               # bulk data leaves in volume
*break_glass*               # [forward] emergency override of access controls
*emergency_access*          # emergency access to records
*export*                    # data leaving: bulk, EHI, VAERS and QRDA exports and their ownership
*ehi_*                      # electronic health information (ONC 170.315(b)(10))
*disclos*                   # disclosures and the accounting of them
*reportab*                  # public-health (eCR) reportability data leaving
*referral_origination*      # referrals originated to other organizations
*bh_access_clock*           # behavioral-health access-to-care timing (Part 2 adjacent)

# --- audit and PHI handling ---
*audit*                     # the PHI access trail
*phi_*                      # PHI sanitising and handling
*encrypt*                   # encryption and its verification
*breach*                    # breach detection and notification
*incident*                  # security incidents
*amend*                     # a patient's right to amend their record

# --- tenant boundary ---
*organization*              # the organization/tenant boundary (ADR 0007)
*tenant*                    # [forward] tenant stamping and isolation

# --- money ---
*billing*                   # [forward] money
*claim*                     # [forward] claims
*payment*                   # [forward] payments
*invoice*                   # [forward] invoices

# --- views that carry more than display ---
app/views/layouts/*         # the layout emits the CSRF and CSP meta tags
app/views/*/patient_contexts/*   # the form that binds a session to a patient (the cross-patient guard)

# --- decisions and compliance record ---
docs/adr/*                  # architecture decisions that bind later work
docs/compliance/*           # compliance posture and disclosure audits
docs/certification/*        # certification evidence
SOFTWARE-FACTORY*           # [forward] the review method itself

# ======================================================================================
# THE SAFE-LIST. Add a glob only for a path where a mistake cannot change who may see what
# or what is stored: prose, markup that only displays, styling. Never code that decides,
# controllers, services, models, serializers, tests, features, db, config or CI. Prefer
# a narrow extension to a directory.
# ======================================================================================
[safe]
README.md                   # prose
CHANGELOG.md                # [forward] prose
docs/*.md                   # prose (docs/adr, docs/compliance and docs/certification are laptop-only rules above)
app/views/*.erb             # display templates (the layout, sign-in and patient-context views are laptop-only rules above)
app/helpers/*.rb            # view helpers
app/assets/stylesheets/*.css   # styling
app/assets/images/*.png     # [forward] images
app/assets/images/*.jpg     # [forward] images
app/assets/images/*.jpeg    # [forward] images
app/assets/images/*.gif     # [forward] images
app/assets/images/*.ico     # [forward] images
config/locales/*.yml        # [forward] display strings
